LESSON: WAVES

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Natural Physical Science
Topic 3.3: Waves
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Waves, part of Natural Physical Science in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How are waves applicable in our day-to-day life? 2. How do waves affect our environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use print or non-print media to research on the terms used in waves and properties of waves (wavelength, period, amplitude, frequency and velocity) and present in the plenary. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or use adapted digital devices or be supported by peers, learner support assistants or teachers as they use print or non-print media to research. Light intensity should be controlled for learners who are photosensitive,

2. discuss with peers the interpretation of the wave equation by relating the characteristics of the wave and share in the plenary. Learners 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use print or non-print media to research on the terms used in waves and properties of waves (wavelength, period, amplitude, frequency and velocity) and present in the plenary. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or use adapted digital devices or be supported by peers, learner support assistants or teachers as they use print or non-print media to research. Light intensity should be controlled for learners who are photosensitive,
2. discuss with peers the interpretation of the wave equation by relating the characteristics of the wave and share in the plenary. Learners 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Waves together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: as the learner searches for information on applications of reflection, refraction and diffraction of

waves.

69

● Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner searches for information on mitigation measures of the effects of

waves on the environment (communities, ecosystems, infrastructure and operations).

70

Values:
Unity: as the learners play different roles when carrying out experiments to investigate reflection of sound waves using

the echo method.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Safety and security: as the learner appreciates some of the applications of waves related to safety in transport.

● Environmental issues: as the learner searches for information on the effect of waves on the environment

(communities, marine ecosystems, infrastructure and operations).

Suggested Learning Resources:

Textbooks, Physics lab resources (such as Loudspeaker, Measure tape, Stop watch), Online resources, educational

videos, interactive simulations, adapted digital devices, Local environment, Adapted writing resources,
